source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_original: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras / dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_english: From this they fear and desire, they grieve and rejoice, and do not discern the air, shut in by darkness and a blind prison.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Possumus quatuor cornua, quae regnaverunt contra populum Dei, et quatuor accipere, quae eruditi non verbum de verbo exprimentes passiones, sed perturbationes interpretantur, aegritudinem animi et gaudium: duo praesentia, et duo futura, metum et cupiditatem, de quibus et illustris poeta significat: Hinc metuunt, cupiuntque, dolent, gaudentque.
reuse.text_original: Possumus quatuor cornua, quae regnaverunt contra populum Dei, et quatuor πάθη accipere, quae eruditi non verbum de verbo exprimentes κακοζήλως passiones, sed perturbationes interpretantur, aegritudinem animi et gaudium: duo praesentia, et duo futura, metum et cupiditatem, de quibus et illustris poeta significat: Hinc metuunt, cupiuntque, dolent, gaudentque.
reuse.text_english: We can take the four horns, which ruled against the people of God, also as the four things which learned men, not rendering word for word, interpret as passions rather than disturbances: sorrow of soul and joy, two present and two future, fear and desire, concerning which even the famous poet says: Hence they fear, desire, grieve, and rejoice.
